description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Platform: iOS/macOS. Current palette uses white backgrounds, light gray body text and red versus green dots as the only route-status meaning. Selected route is indicated by a slightly darker red. Exact color values are not provided.

# Apple HIG: Perception, meaning and adaptable presentation

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the actual barrier or design decision: readability, visual hierarchy, imagery meaning, movement, locale, privacy or spatial placement. Choose the corresponding topic procedure rather than loading every foundation.
2. For text access, combine Typography with Accessibility only where size, reflow or reading alternatives matter. Use VoiceOver when grouping, semantics or navigation needs a procedure of its own.
3. For color/material decisions, separate content hierarchy from controls and evaluate the actual appearance/background/settings context. Preserve semantic meaning when appearance changes.
4. Deliver prioritized evidence-backed corrections or a concrete presentation specification. Distinguish inspected contrast/layout evidence from runtime and assistive-technology checks still needed.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification
or patch. Load related topics only when the chosen procedure calls for them.

name: apple-hig-color
description: Use when choosing or reviewing Apple-platform color semantics, custom palettes, contrast, Liquid Glass tint, color profiles, or cross-appearance color behavior.

# Assign color by meaning and viewing context

Read [Color](../../references/color.md). Inspect the actual foreground/background pairs, semantic roles, assets, appearances, and supported platforms. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Record unknown rendered colors instead of inventing contrast measurements. Preserve the current stack while expressing the requested palette or implementation change.

Classify each color as content, interactive accent, state, text, separator, or background hierarchy. Reuse semantic system roles where they fit; do not borrow a separator color for text or copy dated RGB swatches into production constants. Keep meanings consistent and pair important color distinctions with words/shapes/icons.

For custom colors, specify light/dark and increased-contrast variants, including local glass appearances even in a single-appearance app. Inspect resting and scrolled compositions against real underlying content. On glass, keep ordinary labels/symbols monochrome and tint sparingly for primary action or important status; prefer a colored primary-button background to colored button text.

Branch by context: honor user accents on Mac, use motion/scale as well as color for TV focus, check visionOS glass against varied surroundings without isolated glaring elements in darkness, and keep Watch complications useful in a single-color tint. For image fidelity, preserve embedded profiles and choose sRGB or appropriate wide-gamut assets based on actual display tests; do not assume two close P3 colors survive sRGB conversion.

**Before → decision → after:** A finance graph uses red/green lines and the same green for inactive labels and a Buy button. Decision: distinguish data from interactivity and retain meaning without hue. After, named/dashed series accompany color, neutral semantic labels describe values, and one accent marks the actionable control, with appearance-specific tested variants.

Deliver a role-to-color mapping plus corrected artifact. Fail if a noninteractive element resembles a link, a state disappears without color, or measured text/icon contrast falls short of the applicable guide. Report calculator inputs/results; hardware, ambient-light, TV-brand, or spatial-background claims require actual checks.

Continue with [Dark Mode](../apple-hig-dark-mode/SKILL.md) for appearance transitions, [Materials](../apple-hig-materials/SKILL.md) for glass surfaces, or [Accessibility](../apple-hig-accessibility/SKILL.md) for broader sensory access.

name: apple-hig-dark-mode

# Adapt the hierarchy to appearance

Read [Dark Mode](../../references/dark-mode.md). Inspect supported platforms, semantic colors, elevated surfaces, asset variants, and live-switch behavior. This guide covers iOS/iPadOS/macOS/tvOS and marks visionOS/watchOS unsupported; do not impose its appearance model on those platforms. Choose design, review, or adaptation mode and distinguish rendered evidence from a proposed palette.

Start from system appearance rather than duplicating it with an app-only switch. If a permanently dark media context is proposed, establish the reason; do not turn that exception into a default for ordinary tasks. Define what happens when appearance changes while a sheet, selection, or text field is active.

Replace literal light/dark fills with semantic surface/text roles or matched custom color sets. Preserve base-versus-elevated distinction on iOS/iPadOS rather than mechanically inverting every value. Check custom glyph outlines and full-color artwork in both modes: reuse an asset if it works, otherwise provide variants under one identity. Reduce a bright image's harsh glow only when necessary without distorting its content.

Test Increase Contrast and Reduce Transparency independently and together. Use the guide's contrast targets for this scope; record actual color pairs and measurements. For Mac desktop tinting, a neutral custom surface may share subtle transparency, but colored states should not change meaning as wallpaper moves behind them.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a notes app inverts its white page to black but leaves fixed gray placeholder text and a white imported diagram. Decision: hierarchy and readable content must adapt together. After, system text/surface roles define the editor, elevated panels remain distinguishable, and a mode-appropriate diagram treatment avoids a glaring rectangle while preserving information.

Deliver corrected appearance tokens/assets or a review with precise failing pairs. Fail if runtime switching leaves a light-only element, an elevated panel merges into its parent, or accessibility settings reduce readability. A static palette cannot verify native vibrancy or desktop tinting; list those checks as pending.

Use [Color](../apple-hig-color/SKILL.md) for semantic role selection and [Images](../apple-hig-images/SKILL.md) when the problem lies in asset production.

name: apple-hig-accessibility
description: Use when designing, reviewing, or adapting Apple-platform interfaces for text enlargement, sensory access, assistive input, motor access, cognitive needs, or accessibility preferences.

# Make the task accessible

Read [Accessibility guidance](../../references/accessibility.md) before applying platform values. This procedure turns that guidance into task-level changes; its artifact format and prioritization are application engineering advice, not additional Apple requirements.

## Establish what can be evaluated

Identify the supported platform, the person's task from entry to completion, and whether the request is design, review, or adaptation. Inspect the supplied screens, content, interaction description, semantics, or implementation. Record which evidence exists: a screenshot can establish visible labels and geometry, but cannot establish spoken names, focus order, alternative activation, or preference behavior. Continue using explicit assumptions when the platform or behavior is missing; ask only when the choice changes the requested result.

For a review, connect each finding to an observed barrier and its consequence for that task. Separate untested behavior needing verification from confirmed defects. For a design or adaptation, change the authorized artifact itself: a revised screen specification, interaction contract, or implementation. A general accessibility checklist alone is not the deliverable.

## Remove the barriers that the task contains

Trace the task without assuming sight, hearing, fine motor control, speech, or fast responses. Select the applicable branches:

- **Reading and visual distinctions:** Preserve content and available actions when text enlarges. Use the guide's platform-specific text defaults and minima; its resizing guidance is at least 200%, with 140% stated for watchOS. Reflow or expose another usable arrangement rather than clipping essential labels. Pair color distinctions with text, shape, or symbols. Evaluate actual foreground/background combinations in light and dark appearances; use a contrast calculator and preserve the guide's stated contrast-table scope instead of claiming that its values alone establish conformance. If the default scheme falls short, specify the Increase Contrast treatment.
- **Information carried by sound or imagery:** Identify what information would disappear when sound or sight is unavailable. Choose captions for synchronized audible events, subtitles for dialogue translation, audio description for visual events, or transcripts for a complete text account according to the content. Specify descriptions for meaningful interface/content imagery and omit redundant decoration. Pair essential sound feedback with a perceivable visual or appropriate haptic equivalent.
- **Manipulation and navigation:** Distinguish visible control size from its actual activation area and separation. Use the guide's platform default as the starting point; its smaller minimum is not a blanket recommendation for dense controls. Replace essential complex or repeated gestures with a labeled onscreen action. Make the complete task navigable and activatable with the supported keyboard and assistive input paths; speech must not be necessary. Preserve system accessibility shortcuts. For custom controls, specify names, roles, values, states, and task order rather than assuming their appearance supplies semantics.
- **Time, motion, and comprehension:** Give people time to read and act; prefer explicit dismissal when transient content requires attention. If motion is present, define a Reduce Motion version that retains state and meaning while reducing automatic movement, bounce, zoom, or depth changes. If media autoplays, provide playback control and consider a global preference; honor Dim Flashing Lights where applicable. Keep the task's navigation and wording consistent rather than adding instructional clutter.

Apply the relevant platform condition. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks with one interaction per screen and the source's two confirmations for difficult-to-reverse actions in that mode. For visionOS, keep controls in comfortable view, avoid head-locked content and repeated large gestures, and accommodate hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. These conditions do not apply automatically to every platform.

## Deliver and check the result

Return the revised artifact or evidence-based review, including the barrier, the concrete change, and its acceptance check. State which platform/preferences were considered and which claims remain unverified. Prioritize blockers to completing the task over cosmetic refinements.

Exercise each selected alternative along the same entry-to-completion path. Fail the check if essential content or actions disappear at the specified text scale, information remains available through only one sense, a required gesture has no equivalent, focus cannot reach/activate a necessary control, or a requested motion accommodation removes meaning. Measure contrast and activation geometry when the evidence permits; report missing measurements rather than inventing them. Use Accessibility Inspector and relevant VoiceOver, Switch Control, Full Keyboard Access, AssistiveTouch, or Pointer Control tests on supported Apple environments. Static inspection or a Linux run cannot establish those runtime results, Apple-device comfort, or App Store Accessibility Nutrition Label eligibility.

## Worked transformation

**Before:** An iPad astronomy log marks observation quality only with green/red dots, announces saving with a chime, and exposes Delete only by a two-finger gesture.

**Decision:** Logging must remain understandable without color or sound and operable without that gesture. Retain compact rows while making status and actions explicit.

**After:** Each row reads “Clear” or “Clouded” alongside its symbol; saving exposes a persistent “Saved” state; a labeled row action opens Delete. The screen specification includes expanded-text reflow, semantic row status, and keyboard/assistive activation acceptance checks. These are proposed changes until the actual implementation passes those checks; the specification does not claim VoiceOver was tested.

## Continue only where needed

For detailed spoken structure and rotor navigation, use [VoiceOver](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-voiceover/SKILL.md). For text reflow/type choices use [Typography](../apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md); for a motion accommodation use [Motion](../apple-hig-motion/SKILL.md). If spatial comfort dominates the task, use [Spatial layout](../apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md). Keep the task's accessibility acceptance checks when handing off.

# Color Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/color) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. ## Contents - [Best practices](#Best-practices) - [Inclusive color](#Inclusive-color) - [System colors](#System-colors) - [Liquid Glass color](#Liquid-Glass-color) - [Color management](#Color-management) - [Platform considerations](#Platform-considerations) - [Specifications](#Specifications) - [Resources](#Resources) - [Change log](#Change-log) Use color to clarify hierarchy, state, continuity, and identity. Prefer system colors when their semantics fit: they adapt to appearance, vibrancy, and accessibility preferences. ## Best practices Keep each color’s meaning consistent; an interactive tint should not also decorate inert text. Provide light, dark, and increased-contrast variants for custom colors, including both appearances in a single-appearance app because Liquid Glass adapts locally. Test outdoors, in dim rooms, on different hardware and display profiles, and against visionOS physical backgrounds. True Tone changes white point on supported phones/tablets/Macs; media, reading, and game apps can specify white-point adaptivity. Test several HD/4K TV brands. Account for nearby artwork and translucent surfaces when choosing colors. Prefer a system color picker so people get familiar selection and shared saved colors. ## Inclusive color Pair essential color signals with words, shapes, or glyphs. Check text/icon contrast and combinations that can be hard to distinguish. Consider cultural meanings rather than assuming colors convey universal emotions or warnings. ## System colors Use APIs rather than copying numeric system values, which can change by release and environment. Dynamic semantic colors describe purpose, such as label, separator, link, or hierarchical background. Preserve those meanings rather than borrowing separator colors for text or label colors for fills. ## Liquid Glass color Clear glass derives its appearance from the content behind it. Small bars can switch between light and dark with underlying content; labels and symbols normally remain monochrome. Larger surfaces such as sidebars become more opaque to preserve readability. Use tinted glass sparingly for important status or a primary action. To emphasize a primary button, color its background rather than its text or symbol, and avoid coloring several control backgrounds. Over colorful content, prefer monochrome bars or an accent that contrasts clearly; a brand accent works more readily against monochrome content. Check resting and initial layouts for overlap between similarly colored content and controls, not only intermediate scroll states. ## Color management A color model describes components such as RGB/CMYK; a color space defines their gamut, and an embedded profile maps numeric values to actual colors. Embed profiles in images; sRGB is broadly reliable. On a wide-color display, Display P3 can improve photo/video fidelity and visual differentiation. The source recommends Display P3 PNG with 16 bits per channel where appropriate. P3 imagery usually converts well to sRGB, but close colors or gradients can merge or clip; provide color-space-specific asset variants when testing exposes problems. ## Platform considerations ### iOS, iPadOS Use grouped backgrounds for grouped tables, otherwise the ordinary system background family. In each family, primary is the overall view, secondary groups within it, and tertiary groups within secondary content. |Role|UIKit API| |---|---| |Primary through quaternary labels|`label`, `secondaryLabel`, `tertiaryLabel`, `quaternaryLabel`| |Placeholder strings|`placeholderText`| |Translucent divider|`separator`| |Opaque divider|`opaqueSeparator`| |Linked text|`link`| |Ordinary backgrounds, levels 1–3|`systemBackground`, `secondarySystemBackground`, `tertiarySystemBackground`| |Grouped backgrounds, levels 1–3|`systemGroupedBackground`, `secondarySystemGroupedBackground`, `tertiarySystemGroupedBackground`| ### macOS Choose NSColor semantic APIs by the actual role, available in the standard Color panel’s Developer palette. |Role|NSColor API| |---|---| |Text on selection in table/list|`alternateSelectedControlTextColor`| |Alternating rows/columns|`alternatingContentBackgroundColors`| |User accent|`controlAccentColor`| |Browser/table background|`controlBackgroundColor`| |Control surface / enabled text|`controlColor`, `controlTextColor`| |System tint / disabled text|`currentControlTint`, `disabledControlTextColor`| |Find indicator / grid lines|`findHighlightColor`, `gridColor`| |Table header / virtual illumination|`headerTextColor`, `highlightColor`| |Keyboard focus ring|`keyboardFocusIndicatorColor`| |Primary through quaternary label|`labelColor`, `secondaryLabelColor`, `tertiaryLabelColor`, `quaternaryLabelColor`| |Link / placeholder|`linkColor`, `placeholderTextColor`| |Selected content in key view|`selectedContentBackgroundColor`| |Selected control / its text|`selectedControlColor`, `selectedControlTextColor`| |Selected menu text|`selectedMenuItemTextColor`| |Text-selection fill / selected text|`selectedTextBackgroundColor`, `selectedTextColor`| |Divider / raised-object shadow|`separatorColor`, `shadowColor`| |Document background / document text|`textBackgroundColor`, `textColor`| |Behind document|`underPageBackgroundColor`| |Inactive selected content|`unemphasizedSelectedContentBackgroundColor`| |Inactive text-selection fill / text|`unemphasizedSelectedTextBackgroundColor`, `unemphasizedSelectedTextColor`| |Window surface / title-bar text|`windowBackgroundColor`, `windowFrameTextColor`| #### App accent colors Since macOS 11, an app accent can color buttons, selections, and sidebar icons when the user chooses multicolor. Another user-selected accent overrides it, except fixed-color sidebar icons whose specific colors carry meaning. ### tvOS Use a restrained palette related to the app logo while letting content lead. Show focus through scaling and responsive motion as well as color. ### visionOS Physical and virtual colors show through glass. Use color for important relationships or emphasis, preferably in bold text or large areas rather than thin text and tiny details. Balance brightness during immersion: avoid isolated bright, flashing, or moving objects against dark surroundings when eyes have adapted to darkness. ### watchOS Background color can convey context or supporting information, such as a ring’s category. Avoid long-lived full-screen colored backgrounds in workouts or playback. Graphic complications must also work in the wearer’s chosen single-color tinted mode. ## Specifications ### System colors The following dated design-reference values were recovered from the official JSON swatch descriptions in the 2026-10-25 snapshot. Each tuple is an 8-bit RGB triplet. Use the semantic APIs in production instead of hard-coding these values: system colors can change with releases and context. # Dark Mode Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/dark-mode) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Respect system light/dark appearance preferences on iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and tvOS. Dark Mode uses darker backgrounds and lighter foregrounds with purpose-specific contrast, rather than mechanically inverting every color. ## Best practices Avoid a separate app appearance switch that duplicates system settings. Handle automatic appearance changes while the app is running. Test both appearances with Increase Contrast and Reduce Transparency separately and together; increased contrast can expose unexpected low-contrast dark text. A permanently dark presentation is an uncommon exception for contexts such as immersive media where surrounding UI should recede. ## Dark Mode colors Choose semantic adaptive colors and asset-catalog Color Sets for custom bright/dim variants, rather than fixed values. Maintain at least 4.5:1 foreground/background contrast; aim for 7:1 with custom colors, especially small type. Slightly dim white-background images if they glow harshly in a dark interface. ### Icons and images Prefer SF Symbols with dynamic tint or vibrancy. Test full-color art in both modes; reuse one asset when it works, otherwise provide mode-specific versions under one asset name. Custom interface icons may need different outlines to keep their edges readable against light and dark surfaces. ### Text Use the primary through quaternary system label colors. Prefer system text fields/views, which adjust text and vibrancy to their actual background, over drawing text manually. ## Platform considerations No extra tvOS rules are given. This source says Dark Mode is not supported on visionOS or watchOS. ### iOS, iPadOS System backgrounds distinguish dimmer base surfaces from brighter elevated foreground surfaces. Sheets, popovers, multitasking apps, and multiple windows use this difference to clarify depth. Preserve automatic system background adaptation instead of replacing it with a static custom fill. ### macOS With the graphite accent setting, desktop tinting subtly picks up wallpaper color in window backgrounds. A neutral custom component with a visible bezel/background can use some transparency to share that harmony. Avoid transparency in colored states because movement or wallpaper changes would unpredictably alter their meaning-bearing colors. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/dark-mode) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: August 6, 2024.

# Accessibility Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Build an interface people can understand, perceive through different senses, and adapt to their preferred methods. Treat accessibility as a design input and audit with Accessibility Inspector. Evaluate actual support before describing Accessibility Nutrition Labels on the App Store. ## Vision Support text enlargement of at least 200%; the source gives 140% for watchOS. Dynamic Type or equivalent custom resizing must preserve usability. Follow platform defaults/minima when choosing custom styles, and enlarge thin-weight custom fonts further when needed. |Platform|Default text|Minimum text| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| Measure contrast using established calculators such as WCAG or APCA. Apple’s Accessibility Inspector table uses these WCAG-AA guidance values: text up to 17 pt, all weights, 4.5:1; 18 pt at all weights, 3:1; bold text at any size, 3:1. Preserve the table’s stated scope rather than assuming it replaces a separate conformance evaluation. If default colors fall short, Increase Contrast must supply a higher-contrast scheme. Test both light and dark. Prefer semantic system colors that adapt to accessibility preferences. Pair color with shape, icons, or text; red/green and blue/orange distinctions can be difficult. Let people customize chart or character colors where useful. Give VoiceOver meaningful descriptions of interface and content. ## Hearing Make dialogue and important information available without sound. Captions describe audible information in synchrony with media, subtitles present dialogue in a chosen language, audio descriptions narrate otherwise visual events in audio pauses, and transcripts provide a complete text account of audible and visual information. Let people adjust text presentation. Pair sound feedback with matching haptics and visual direction cues, especially for offscreen game or spatial events. Music Haptics and audio graphs on iOS/iPadOS can offer tactile representations of music and data. ## Mobility Use comfortable controls and sufficient separation, not just adequate visible size. |Platform|Default control|Minimum control| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| |macOS|28 × 28 pt|20 × 20 pt| |tvOS|66 × 66 pt|56 × 56 pt| |visionOS|60 × 60 pt|28 × 28 pt| |watchOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| The source suggests around 12 pt padding for bezelled elements and 24 pt outside visible edges for elements without a bezel. Use simple gestures for repeated tasks and offer an onscreen alternative for essential gestures, such as a dismiss button alongside swipe-to-dismiss. Avoid requiring complex multiple-finger or multiple-hand actions. Label controls so Voice Control can target them. Siri/Shortcuts can expose repeated tasks through voice, Action buttons, Home Screen, and Control Center. Test VoiceOver, AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Pointer Control, and Switch Control rather than assuming support. ## Speech Support complete keyboard navigation and Full Keyboard Access; preserve system accessibility shortcuts. Support Switch Control navigation and activation through hardware, controller, and sound inputs such as a click or pop, so speech is never a necessary input method. ## Cognitive Use familiar, simple, consistent navigation and gestures. Prefer explicit dismissal over timed disappearance, allowing time for processing and assistive navigation. Games can offer difficulty, reaction-time, success-criteria, and control-assistance accommodations. Give clear playback controls and consider a global autoplay preference. Respect Dim Flashing Lights during media playback. Honor Reduce Motion by reducing automatic and repeated movement, scaling, zooming, and peripheral effects. Reduce spring bounce; tie appropriate motion directly to gestures; avoid animated depth changes and blur transitions; replace spatial translations with fades. Fast or blinking motion can distract, cause dizziness, or trigger seizures. Keep controls inside a comfortable field of view; horizontal arrangements usually strain the neck less than tall ones. Avoid rapid shifts of attention among distant locations. Reduce peripheral animation speed and intensity, use gentle camera/video motion, and avoid making the surrounding world move without the person’s control. # Transit disruption dashboard: revised interaction specification

## Scope and evidence

This is a framework-agnostic design for iOS and macOS. "'`interface.md` supplies white backgrounds, light-gray body text, red/green status dots, and a slightly darker red for selection. It supplies no RGB values, implementation, screenshot, or interaction details. Contrast failure cannot be measured for that original palette; hue-only status and shade-only selection are confirmed by the brief.

The task is to identify a route'"'s service condition, select it, and read its disruption details. The row/detail interaction and expanded status vocabulary below are proposed product decisions, not observed existing behavior. No Apple SDK is required.

## Decisions and semantic roles

Separate service status, selection, keyboard focus, and action tint. Preserve each meaning across appearance changes. Prefer a host's genuine semantic colors when available; resolve them by purpose rather than copying Apple's dated swatches. Otherwise use the explicit opaque fallback below. These recommendations follow [Color: System colors and Inclusive color](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/color#System-colors).

| Role | Contract |
|---|---|
| "'`surface.canvas` | Overall dashboard surface; use the host'"'s ordinary background hierarchy, or grouped hierarchy if the implementation groups routes. |
| "'`surface.row` | Opaque route-row surface. Status colors are evaluated against this surface. |
| `surface.detail` | Distinct detail surface; retain the host'"'s base/elevated distinction on iOS. |
| "'`text.primary` | Route name, status words, disruption explanation, essential times. Never use separator or disabled colors for these. |
| `text.secondary` | Supporting metadata, such as last updated time; still readable. |
| `separator` | Decorative grouping boundary only; never the sole selection signal. |
| `action.accent` | Interactive actions only. Honor the user'"'s macOS accent preference; do not use that preference to redefine transit severity. |
| "'`selection.outline` | Primary foreground outline plus visible “Selected” text; independent of service status and accent. |
| `focus.outline` | Host focus indicator, or primary-foreground outer ring in fallback. Separate from persistent selection. |
| `status.*` | Fixed semantic category with a word and distinct shape. Never tint the entire row by severity. |

Status mapping is a product taxonomy: `normal` = green circle with check + “Normal service”; `delayed` = amber triangle with exclamation + “Delayed”; `suspended` = red octagon with stop mark + “Service suspended”; `unknown` = neutral diamond with question mark + “Status unavailable”. The data adapter must map documented upstream codes explicitly. An unmapped, missing, or stale status becomes unknown, with a last-updated explanation; it must not imply normal service. The freshness threshold must come from the feed contract and remains unresolved here. Route identity colors, if later added, must stay separate from these status roles.

The icons are generic vector geometry, not SF Symbols requirements. Status words remain visible in monochrome. Shapes can be decorative to assistive technology because the adjacent text carries their full meaning. See [Accessibility: Vision](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility#Vision).

### Concrete fallback color sets

These are proposed custom sRGB values, not Apple system constants. All are opaque. Columns are light, dark, light with Increase Contrast, and dark with Increase Contrast.

| Token | Light | Dark | Light increased | Dark increased |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `surface.canvas` | #F2F4F6 | #101214 | #FFFFFF | #000000 |
| `surface.row`, `surface.detail` | #FFFFFF | #181C20 | #FFFFFF | #101214 |
| `text.primary`, selection/fallback focus outlines | #17212B | #F3F6F8 | #000000 | #FFFFFF |
| `text.secondary` | #465563 | #B9C5D0 | #283440 | #E3EAF0 |
| `status.suspended` | #A31825 | #FFB4B8 | #7C0012 | #FFDADD |
| `status.normal` | #176534 | #8BE0A8 | #004820 | #C4F7D4 |
| `status.delayed` | #805000 | #FFD58A | #603900 | #FFE9BC |
| `status.unknown` | #505C68 | #BAC5CF | #303B46 | #E0E7ED |

Status glyphs use their status foreground on `surface.row`; status words use `text.primary`. Fallback separators use `text.secondary`. Fallback action labels use `text.primary` with a persistent underline; their interactive role does not depend on hue. Native integrations may use adaptive accent/link roles after verifying contrast. No invented fixed blue approximates a user'"'s accent.

Fallback selected rows retain their normal fill and status color, gain a 2 logical-unit inset outline in "'`text.primary`, and display “Selected”. Focus adds a separate 2-unit outer ring with a 2-unit surface-colored gap. Reserve space so rings do not clip. These dimensions are product choices, not HIG numerical requirements. At increased contrast, boundaries remain explicit; do not rely on barely different neutral fills. Fallback detail has a primary-foreground border to distinguish it from its surroundings.

## Interaction and appearance contract

Each route row contains route name, visible status glyph and words, update time, and selection indicator. A single selection activates its detail region. On iOS that region may be a detail destination with Back; on macOS it may be adjacent. Both preserve selected route identity when returning. No separate dot target is needed.

1. Activating a route sets its stable ID as selected, updates the detail content, and exposes the selected state programmatically. The previous row loses its outline and “Selected” text. Status does not change.
2. Keyboard focus alone does not select a route. Tab/host navigation reaches route controls; Enter or Space activates them. Expose an appropriate selectable-control role, route/status name, and selected value through the framework'"'s accessibility layer.
3. Data updates replace the selected route's status text, glyph, and detail together. Keep selection and focus stable; never flash red/green. If the route disappears, clear selection and show “Route no longer available”; do not silently select another route.
4. Follow system appearance, without a duplicate in-app switch. Re-resolve all roles on light/dark or accessibility preference changes, including while a detail destination is active. Preserve selection, focus, navigation, and scroll position; do not reload the feed because appearance changed.
5. Use opaque status surfaces in all settings. Reduce Transparency therefore does not change their meaning or contrast. Do not add glass to this design. A future translucent surface requires a new compositing audit, including resting/scrolled content and local appearance.
6. Allow status words and details to wrap at 200% text enlargement. Selection indicators move to a new line if needed. Do not truncate essential route/status meaning. Start from platform text defaults and comfortable target defaults: iOS 17 pt text and 44 × 44 pt targets; macOS 13 pt text and 28 × 28 pt targets. These are defaults from the supplied guidance, not interchangeable cross-platform minima.

Appearance behavior follows [Dark Mode: Best practices, Dark Mode colors, and platform considerations](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/dark-mode). Input and enlargement requirements follow [Accessibility: Vision, Mobility, and Speech](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility).

"'```text
renderRow(route, state, environment):
    palette = resolveSemanticRoles(environment.appearance,
                                   environment.increaseContrast,
                                   environment.platformAccent)
    status = normalizeFeedStatus(route, feedFreshnessPolicy)
    drawOpaqueRow(palette.surface.row)
    show(route.name, palette.text.primary)
    show(status.shape, palette.status[status.kind])
    show(status.words, palette.text.primary)
    show(route.updateDescription, palette.text.secondary)
    if state.selectedID == route.id:
        drawInsetSelectionOutline()
        show("Selected", palette.text.primary)
    if state.focusedID == route.id: drawSeparateFocusRing()
    exposeSelectableRoute(route.name, status.words, selected)

onAppearanceOrContrastChanged(environment):
    invalidateResolvedColorsForAllVisibleAndCachedSurfaces()
    rerenderPreservingInteractionState()
```

## Worked before/after

Illustrative input: Route 24 has suspended service; Route 7 has normal service; Route 24 is selected.

**Before:** Both rows have white backgrounds and light-gray body text. Route 24 has a red dot, made slightly darker for selection; Route 7 has a green dot. Without hue, neither service condition nor selection is reliably expressed. No numeric contrast conclusion is possible.

**After, light fallback:** Route 24 has a #FFFFFF surface, #17212B route name and “Service suspended”, #A31825 octagon, and #17212B outline plus “Selected”. Route 7 has “Normal service” and a #176534 check-circle, without a selection outline. Route 24'"'s detail explicitly says “Service suspended”; any explanation comes from actual feed data.

**Switch to dark while Route 24 is selected:** Row surfaces become #181C20, primary text/outlines #F3F6F8, suspended glyph #FFB4B8, and normal glyph #8BE0A8. Route 24 stays selected with its detail and scroll position intact. Turning Increase Contrast on resolves the dark-increased column. Even when all colors are rendered gray, words, shapes, and the selection outline preserve the same task information.

## Acceptance checks and observed results

**Passed — specification/static evidence:** Every status has words and shape; selection is independent of severity; all fallback custom roles have four variants; live appearance changes preserve interaction state by contract. These establish specification completeness, not implemented behavior.

**Passed — numerical fallback calculation:** A headless Python 3 calculation used WCAG relative luminance for opaque sRGB: linearize each channel, compute "'`L = .2126R + .7152G + .0722B`, then `(lighter L + .05)/(darker L + .05)`. Inputs are exactly the row-background and foreground hex values above. Ratios below are ordered primary, secondary, suspended, normal, delayed, unknown:

| Mode / background | Calculated ratios |
|---|---|
| Light / #FFFFFF | 16.29, 7.66, 7.74, 7.12, 6.85, 6.84 |
| Dark / #181C20 | 15.78, 9.76, 10.18, 10.87, 12.35, 9.77 |
| Light increased / #FFFFFF | 21.00, 12.69, 11.26, 10.78, 10.08, 11.41 |
| Dark increased / #101214 | 18.77, 15.46, 14.59, 15.74, 15.76, 15.04 |

All calculated pairs exceed 4.5:1. The local Dark Mode guide recommends at least 4.5:1 and aiming for 7:1 with custom colors, especially small text. Light delayed/unknown glyphs fall below that aspirational 7:1; their accompanying small text uses primary foreground, which exceeds it. The Accessibility guide'"'s separate Inspector table has size/weight qualifications; this specification chooses the stricter 4.5:1 floor for all these pairs rather than treating the table as blanket conformance.

**Failed — supplied design's semantic redundancy:** Red/green dots alone and darker red selection do not convey their meanings independently of color. The revised contract corrects this; implementation is still pending. No original measured contrast failure is asserted.

**Not executed — implementation acceptance gates:**

- Exercise select → inspect detail → appearance switch → contrast switch → Back. Same route, status, focus, and reading position must persist; no light-only cached elements may remain.
- Repeat all four appearance/contrast combinations with Reduce Transparency off/on. Verify actual rendered text, glyph, outline, action, and selected/focused pairs on every real surface; minimum 4.5:1 for the specified essential foregrounds. Host semantic colors and composited pixels need their own measurements.
- In grayscale, distinguish every status, selection, and keyboard focus without consulting color. Verify macOS user accents, inactive-window selection, and wallpaper changes do not redefine status or hide selection.
- At 200% text size, all essential words and actions remain available without overlap or clipping. Measure actual platform target geometry and ring clearance.
- Complete route selection/detail/back using keyboard and supported assistive input. Verify accessible name, role, selected value, focus visibility/order, and no duplicate decorative-glyph announcements on actual iOS/macOS environments.
- Inspect light/dark hierarchy and glyph outlines on devices in bright and dim environments and relevant display profiles. A fallback palette calculation cannot establish these results.

## Evidence limits and source audit

Only supplied local files and installed instructions were used; no web requests were made. Official links identify the source articles, not independently verified current guidance. The installed references are application guidance based on an Apple HIG snapshot retrieved 2026-10-25, not SDK documentation or proof of independent source review.

Auditable reading route: installed "'`apple-hig/SKILL.md` → `interface.md` → Foundations family → relevant topic-index rows → Color, Dark Mode, and Accessibility topic procedures → their respective source guides. Each file was read in its own shell command. No platform feasibility or SDK integration is claimed.

No application was implemented or run. No device, GUI, SDK compilation, native rendering, accessibility tool, VoiceOver, or physical-environment test was performed. The successful Python 3 calculation verifies only the listed opaque numerical pairs; an initial `python` command was unavailable. Feed status mapping and freshness policy require the actual upstream contract before shipping. The proposed interactions, colors, and checks are ready for implementation, with runtime results explicitly pending.

renderRow(route, state, environment):
    palette = resolveSemanticRoles(environment.appearance,

## Worked before/after

Illustrative input: Route 24 has suspended service; Route 7 has normal service; Route 24 is selected.

**Before:** Both rows have white backgrounds and light-gray body text. Route 24 has a red dot, made slightly darker for selection; Route 7 has a green dot. Without hue, neither service condition nor selection is reliably expressed. No numeric contrast conclusion is possible.

**After, light fallback:** Route 24 has a #FFFFFF surface, #17212B route name and “Service suspended”, #A31825 octagon, and #17212B outline plus “Selected”. Route 7 has “Normal service” and a #176534 check-circle, without a selection outline. Route 24'"'s detail explicitly says “Service suspended”; any explanation comes from actual feed data.

**Switch to dark while Route 24 is selected:** Row surfaces become #181C20, primary text/outlines #F3F6F8, suspended glyph #FFB4B8, and normal glyph #8BE0A8. Route 24 stays selected with its detail and scroll position intact. Turning Increase Contrast on resolves the dark-increased column. Even when all colors are rendered gray, words, shapes, and the selection outline preserve the same task information.

## Acceptance checks and observed results

**Passed — specification/static evidence:** Every status has words and shape; selection is independent of severity; all fallback custom roles have four variants; live appearance changes preserve interaction state by contract. These establish specification completeness, not implemented behavior.

**Passed — numerical fallback calculation:** A headless Python 3 calculation used WCAG relative luminance for opaque sRGB: linearize each channel, compute "'`L = .2126R + .7152G + .0722B`, then `(lighter L + .05)/(darker L + .05)`. Inputs are exactly the row-background and foreground hex values above. Ratios below are ordered primary, secondary, suspended, normal, delayed, unknown:

| Mode / background | Calculated ratios |
|---|---|
| Light / #FFFFFF | 16.29, 7.66, 7.74, 7.12, 6.85, 6.84 |
| Dark / #181C20 | 15.78, 9.76, 10.18, 10.87, 12.35, 9.77 |
| Light increased / #FFFFFF | 21.00, 12.69, 11.26, 10.78, 10.08, 11.41 |
| Dark increased / #101214 | 18.77, 15.46, 14.59, 15.74, 15.76, 15.04 |

All calculated pairs exceed 4.5:1. The local Dark Mode guide recommends at least 4.5:1 and aiming for 7:1 with custom colors, especially small text. Light delayed/unknown glyphs fall below that aspirational 7:1; their accompanying small text uses primary foreground, which exceeds it. The Accessibility guide'"'s separate Inspector table has size/weight qualifications; this specification chooses the stricter 4.5:1 floor for all these pairs rather than treating the table as blanket conformance.

**Failed — supplied design's semantic redundancy:** Red/green dots alone and darker red selection do not convey their meanings independently of color. The revised contract corrects this; implementation is still pending. No original measured contrast failure is asserted.

**Not executed — implementation acceptance gates:**

- Exercise select → inspect detail → appearance switch → contrast switch → Back. Same route, status, focus, and reading position must persist; no light-only cached elements may remain.
- Repeat all four appearance/contrast combinations with Reduce Transparency off/on. Verify actual rendered text, glyph, outline, action, and selected/focused pairs on every real surface; minimum 4.5:1 for the specified essential foregrounds. Host semantic colors and composited pixels need their own measurements.
- In grayscale, distinguish every status, selection, and keyboard focus without consulting color. Verify macOS user accents, inactive-window selection, and wallpaper changes do not redefine status or hide selection.
- At 200% text size, all essential words and actions remain available without overlap or clipping. Measure actual platform target geometry and ring clearance.
- Complete route selection/detail/back using keyboard and supported assistive input. Verify accessible name, role, selected value, focus visibility/order, and no duplicate decorative-glyph announcements on actual iOS/macOS environments.
- Inspect light/dark hierarchy and glyph outlines on devices in bright and dim environments and relevant display profiles. A fallback palette calculation cannot establish these results.

## Evidence limits and source audit

Only supplied local files and installed instructions were used; no web requests were made. Official links identify the source articles, not independently verified current guidance. The installed references are application guidance based on an Apple HIG snapshot retrieved 2026-10-25, not SDK documentation or proof of independent source review.

Auditable reading route: installed "'`apple-hig/SKILL.md` → `interface.md` → Foundations family → relevant topic-index rows → Color, Dark Mode, and Accessibility topic procedures → their respective source guides. Each file was read in its own shell command. No platform feasibility or SDK integration is claimed.
